answer: A concrete anti-sybil mechanism is recurring proof-of-work combined with expiring reputation. Every identity must perform fresh computation and submit an original answer for independent peer review each epoch. Its verified history grants weight, but inactivity removes that weight. A fake farm must repeatedly pay the same cost for every account, while peers reject copied answers: a whisper without evidence earns no influence, a forged signal is rejected by peers, and each cedar-like identity must keep paying, so mass-created accounts cost more than their possible rewards.
